img_to_rgb — 2D bridge op

• Data kinds: image → rgbimage

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "img_to_rgb", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

Give a gray image a hue and saturation, producing an (H,W,3) RGB image (sort rgbimage).

Built in the form of the dichromatic reflection model (diffuse = coloured, specular = white):

mix = (1 - sat) + sat * chroma, chroma = HSV(hue, 1, 1), spec = clip((gray - 0.75) / 0.25, 0, 1) ** 2, rgb = gray * (mix * (1 - spec) + spec). In other words, dark to mid-tone pixels are coloured by the hue, and the further a pixel's brightness exceeds 0.75, the more it returns to white (achromatic). With saturation 0 it is a grey with 3 equal channels (the input itself, regardless of spec). Every channel is at or below the input, so the range stays within [0,1].

• a → hue hue = a (red at 0, green at 1/3, blue at 2/3, back to red at 1).

• b → saturation sat = b (coloured only halfway at b=0.5).

• Returns: (H, W, 3) float64.

• The specular knee SPECULAR_KNEE = 0.75 is fixed (not made a knob).

Why specular is included (measured 2026-09-07): with simple colouring gray * mix the bright parts also become a saturated colour of the same hue, and the "achromatic highlights" that tb_specular_coefficient_map / tb_specular_diffuse_split / tb_specular_free_transform look at did not exist on even 1 pixel, so the specular coefficient was all 0 and the figure pitch black. The synthesis input side satisfies the family's assumption (dichromatic).

Where to use: tb_rgb_to_quaternion (→ qimage, the entry to the quaternion colour ops), tb_specular_free_transform / tb_wetness / tb_sensor_capture. It does not reproduce the colours of natural images (a single-hue synthesis).
